metadata.title: Hydrogen Atom — Energy Levels & Transitions (Viz Riff)
metadata.purpose: Critique the D3 hydrogen energy-level diagram — encodings, interaction, selection-rule honesty

beats.narration_text: Bonjour. Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude to build a hydrogen energy level diagram — click two levels, get a verdict on the transition. We judge the visualization. Not the physics.

props.segment: Judge the Viz, Not the Physics
props.command: write me a D3 visualization of hydrogen atom energy levels and radiative transitions — click any two n,ℓ levels to check the electric-dipole selection rule
output: ✓ Energy level diagram — n = 1–6, ℓ sublevels

beats.narration_text: Left panel: a linear energy axis from minus thirteen-point-six to zero electron-volts. Tick marks for each n-ℓ sublevel, n equals one through six, in four columns — s, p, d, f. Arrows pre-drawn for the major series: Lyman in purple, Balmer color-matched to wavelength, Paschen in dark red. Right: a log-scale emission spectrum from ninety to two-thousand nanometers, and a physics-checks console.
beats.new_visual_element: output.mp4 full clip — baseline diagram, pre-drawn arrows

beats.narration_text: Click a first level, click a second — the sim draws a transition arrow and delivers a verdict: ALLOWED or FORBIDDEN. The info box shows the transition notation, delta-E in eV, wavelength in nm, and the delta-ell value. Clicking four-d then two-p: allowed emission at four-eighty-six nanometers, Hβ. Clicking two-s then one-s: forbidden — delta-ell equals zero. The mechanism the sim enforces is the electric-dipole selection rule: delta-ell must be plus or minus one.
beats.new_visual_element: change.mp4 full clip — click-through showing allowed emission (Hβ, Hα) and forbidden (2s→1s)

beats.narration_text: Two things this gets right. First: the two-click structure forces commitment before feedback — the correct structure for teaching a rule. You choose both endpoints before the verdict appears. Second: the log scale on the spectrum. It gives Lyman, Balmer, and Paschen roughly equal horizontal space, matching how the series converge. And when you select Ly-alpha, the info box includes the spontaneous emission lifetime — one-point-six nanoseconds. Data, not decoration.
beats.new_visual_element: still from change.mp4 at t=4.3 — 4d→2p info box showing allowed emission verdict

beats.narration_text: Two things this gets wrong. The energy axis is linear in eV, and hydrogen levels scale as one-over-n-squared. So n equals four, five, and six are squeezed into the top fifteen percent of the diagram — pixel-scale targets. The fix is a one-over-n-squared axis that spaces the levels uniformly. Also: the subtitle announces three selection rules, including delta-m equals zero or plus-minus one. The code checks one of them. A student reading the subtitle thinks m matters. The sim cannot show it. Remove delta-m, or represent m-states.
beats.new_visual_element: still from output.mp4 at t=2 — initial state showing crowded n=4–6 levels at top

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Useful for upper-division quantum mechanics — the click-two-levels structure is right, the log spectrum is the right call, the info box gives real numbers. Replace the linear axis with a one-over-n-squared scale. Remove the delta-m selection rule from the subtitle — or represent m-states.

artifactLines: Log scale on the spectrum: correct call.
Linear axis crowds n=4–6 into pixels — switch to 1/n².
Δm in the subtitle, never in the code — remove it.

beats.narration_text: I have a D3 hydrogen energy-level diagram. It plots energy on a linear eV axis, which crowds n=4 through n=6 into the top fifteen percent of the diagram. Rewrite the y-scale to a one-over-n-squared spacing so that n=1 through n=6 are evenly distributed vertically. Keep the existing energy labels in eV at each level, the pre-drawn transition arrows, and the click-two-levels selection-rule interaction. The SVG viewport is three-ninety by five-hundred pixels.
